summary: Status as of Oct 6, 2026, 18:00 UTC: the story is at its peak in mainstream news. Search interest is very high: Wikipedia "Plague (disease)" is getting about 36k views a day and is new in the top 1000. Many explainer pieces are out (AP, BBC, CNN, PBS, Axios, Guardian, Atlantic), and broadcasters (NBC, Fox, news channels) have posted YouTube explainers. The official picture has also changed. Plague is NOT confirmed. Rospotrebnadzor (Russia's health watchdog) says tests on the woman who died found no microorganisms linked to her lab work. It also says contacts showed no plague (2 COVID-19 and 2 rhinovirus infections only). Russian authorities call the cause 'pneumonia of unknown origin' and deny a lab accident. WHO's initial assessment: risk moderate to low for Irkutsk, low for Russia, very low for the WHO European region. The US (State Department/CDC) is monitoring and has asked for more information. A 'second death' report from UNITED24 has not been verified and must not be amplified. Our edge is not being first with the news. It is being the calm, dated decoder that separates confirmed from reported from denied, plus search-intent Plague 101 answers (is it contagious, is it like COVID, is it curable, symptoms, US cases). Every status piece must be re-checked against WHO and Rospotrebnadzor at publish time, because the confirmation could still go either way.

candidates.topic: Irkutsk 'plague' case decoded: what's confirmed, reported and denied (as of Oct 6, 2026). Russia says no plague found in contacts; WHO rates the risk low.
candidates.angle: A three-column status decoder: CONFIRMED (one lab worker died of severe pneumonia; contacts under observation; WHO rates the risk low for Russia and very low for Europe) / REPORTED (regional outlets say a test tube broke; suspected pneumonic plague) / OFFICIAL RUSSIAN POSITION (Rospotrebnadzor: no work-related microbes found in her samples; contacts tested negative for plague; 'pneumonia of unknown origin'). End with what would change the picture and the 'talk to a health professional' line. Dated, calm, no doom.
candidates.predicted_peak: now–3 days (re-peaks on any WHO/Rospotrebnadzor update)
candidates.why_now: Dozens of outlets published on Oct 6, and the official status shifted the same day: Russia told WHO there is no plague in contacts, and WHO gave its risk assessment. People are searching 'is it confirmed'. Decoders are our most repeatable formula (3 for 3).

candidates.angle: Answer in 10 seconds: yes, but mainly through close, face-to-face contact with someone who is coughing and very ill (droplets), not across rooms like measles. Explain why that makes contact tracing work. Name the comparator outright.

candidates.topic: Is plague curable? Antibiotics work when started early, the treatment window explained (CDC/WHO)
candidates.angle: A calm, myth-correcting answer: plague is treatable with common antibiotics, and starting early is what matters most, especially for pneumonic plague. Use CDC/WHO fatality figures for treated vs untreated cases, with attribution. No drug names with doses, no stockpiling or self-treatment. If exposed or ill: urgent care or the local health authority.
candidates.why_now: The death raised a 'there's no cure' fear. It's an evergreen search question, and the news has pushed it to a spike.

evidence.signal: Antibiotic treatment; early treatment is key
Untreated pneumonic plague is usually fatal; treatable when caught early

candidates.topic: Plague in the US: about 7 human cases a year (CDC), where they happen, and the role of fleas, pets and wildlife
candidates.angle: Bring it close to home for our US-heavy audience: rural parts of the western US (Southwest: NM, AZ, CO; CA, OR, NV), rodent fleas, and cats as a source. Practical prevention: flea control for pets, don't handle sick or dead wildlife, see a doctor fast if symptoms appear after exposure. Calm and concrete.

candidates.topic: Bubonic vs septicemic vs pneumonic plague: the three forms of Yersinia pestis, and why only pneumonic passes between people
candidates.angle: Plague 101 comparison. Bubonic: flea bite, swollen lymph node. Septicemic: bloodstream. Pneumonic: lungs, and the only form that spreads person to person. Visual: flea → lymph node → blood → lungs. Use clean diagrams, no graphic imagery.
candidates.why_now: Wikipedia's plague page jumped to about 36k views a day. People are learning the basics, and 'pneumonic' is a new word for most of them.

candidates.topic: Pneumonic plague symptoms and timing: what to watch for and when to get urgent care
candidates.angle: Symptoms (CDC: fever, headache, weakness, fast-developing pneumonia with shortness of breath, chest pain, cough) and incubation (about 1–3 days for pneumonic). The key point: the risk depends on exposure. For most viewers a cough is not plague. Urgent care only with symptoms plus a real exposure (plague area, sick animals, a known contact).
